Good Tuesday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 613 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Amy Stern for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Meet the flying medic
 
Photo: Pivotal

A paramedic responding to a recent 911 call in coastal North Carolina piloted a "Jetsons"-like aircraft to the scene, Axios' Joann Muller reports.

  • It landed right in the patient's yard, about 20 minutes before ground ambulances arrived.
  • That fast airborne response offers a glimpse of the future of emergency medical care in rural America, where hospitals are far away and time is critical.

🚁 Hyde County officials say they're the first in the U.S. to use an eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft) for real 911 calls.

  • Flight-trained paramedic Quinn Reece is flying a BlackFly ultralight plane, carrying first-response gear to help stabilize patients before ground EMTs can get to the scene.
The Pivotal BlackFly in flight. Photo: Pivotal

The single-passenger BlackFly is a simple, lightweight design.

  • It can take off and land vertically on pavement, dirt or grass.
  • If something goes wrong, a parachute can carry the 254-pound aircraft safely to the ground.

🚑 Reece said her biggest takeaway from the project is "seeing how these new aircraft can change the way we think about emergency response, especially in rural communities."

2. 🤖 AI could help unlock more oil — and emissions
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

AI could help produce more oil and natural gas — but with a climate impact outweighing the tech's benefits for renewable energy, Axios' Amy Harder reports from a new study.

🛢️ The big picture: AI can help oil companies find new resources and extract more from existing fields.

  • At the same time, it can also improve forecasting and operations for renewables.

🌎 What they found: The researchers estimate that AI could add emissions equal to roughly 1% to 5% of the global energy sector's 2024 total.

Co-author Holly Alpine tells Axios: "Most assessments of AI's climate impact are framed as a trade-off between data center energy use and the emissions AI might help avoid through renewables and efficiency gains."

  • "What's missing from that calculation entirely is the other side of the same ledger: the emissions enabled from using AI to make fossil fuel production cheaper and more profitable."

American Petroleum Institute spokeswoman Andrea Woods tells Axios: "The U.S. oil and natural gas industry is continuing to produce more energy while reducing emissions by investing in better technology, implementing stronger operational practices and supporting science-based policy."

4. 🎮 1 for the road: Madden meets AI
 
A screengrab from franchise mode. Photo: EA

Madden NFL 27's refreshed franchise mode features AI-generated breaking news, headlines and media narratives, Axios' Herb Scribner reports.

  • Instead of selecting a task like "pick your rookie class," players will open up a generated article titled: "Which rookies will we see in the NFL draft?"

🏈 A "news center" shows gamers what's happening around the league.

  • During the offseason, players will enter a "free agent frenzy" mini-game with breaking news alerts from ESPN.
